trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the L9 Sud metro line to Torrassa, then transfer to reach Sant Just Desvern area (budget option ~€5.15 with T-Casual card). Check in to Sercotel Porta Barcelona. Once settled, take a short stroll around the local neighbourhood to get oriented and grab a light bite nearby.

meals.lunch: N/A – in transit or airport snack
meals.dinner: Bar/restaurant near the hotel in Sant Just Desvern – look for a local 'menú del día' or a neighbourhood tapas bar. Budget ~€8–12 for a simple set meal or bocadillo with a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€11.35) at the airport – it will save money throughout the trip. Keep the first evening light as it will be a long travel day. Temperatures around 28°C in the evening so dress light.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café, then head into central Barcelona via metro. Start with the Gothic Quarter Architecture Walk – a self-guided tour through Barri Gòtic discovering Roman ruins, medieval palaces, the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and hidden alleyways. Pick up a free map at the tourist office or use a free app like Google Maps with offline mode. This is completely free and best enjoyed in the cooler morning hours (9:00–12:00).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from the Gothic Quarter along La Rambla to the waterfront (La Barceloneta). Cool off with a dip at Barceloneta Beach (free). Explore the Port Olímpic area on foot. Grab lunch at a local chiringuito or a supermarket (Mercadona/Lidl) for a budget picnic on the beach. Rest during the hottest part of the day (14:00–16:00). In the late afternoon, visit the free exterior of the Palau de la Música Catalana and wander El Born neighbourhood.
day_by_day.evening: Head to El Born or the Gothic Quarter for pre-dinner drinks. Many bars offer free tapas with a drink during happy hour (18:00–20:00). Dinner in El Born, then explore the neighbourhood's bar scene – Bar del Pla and El Xampanyet are local favourites. The area comes alive after 22:00 for nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Café con leche and a croissant or tostada at a local café near the hotel – budget ~€3–4
meals.lunch: Supermarket picnic on Barceloneta Beach or a bocadillo from a local bakery – budget ~€5–7
meals.dinner: Set menú del día or tapas in El Born neighbourhood – budget ~€10–14. Try Bar del Pla for affordable Catalan tapas.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – the Gothic Quarter has uneven cobblestones. Carry a refillable water bottle; public drinking fountains are available throughout the city. Sun protection is essential at 28°C+.

day_by_day.morning: Book the Sagrada Família Guided Tour in advance online (cheaper than at the door; standard entry ~€26, with tower access ~€36). Arrive at opening time (9:00) to beat the crowds. The guided tour with tower access offers panoramic views of the city and an in-depth look at Gaudí's architectural genius. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Sagrada Família, walk or take the metro to Gràcia neighbourhood. Explore the free exterior of Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) along Passeig de Gràcia – the 'Block of Discord' is a free architecture feast from the outside. Walk up to Parc Güell: the monumental zone requires a ticket (~€10, book online), but the surrounding park and viewpoints are free and offer stunning city views. Spend the hottest hours (14:00–17:00) resting in the shaded park areas.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gràcia neighbourhood for the evening – it has a vibrant local nightlife scene with many affordable bars and terraces. Vermouth hour ('vermut') starts around 19:00. After dinner, explore the lively squares like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia, which fill with locals socialising well into the night.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee at a bakery near the hotel before heading out – budget ~€3–4
meals.lunch: Picnic in Parc Güell with supermarket supplies, or a budget bocadillo from a nearby café in Gràcia – budget ~€5–8
meals.dinner: Affordable tapas or a menú del día in Gràcia – try La Pepita or a local neighbourhood restaurant. Budget ~€10–14.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tickets at least a few days in advance – they sell out fast, especially in August. Book Parc Güell monumental zone tickets online too (~€10). Total architecture spend today ~€36–46 but these are the trip highlights worth the splurge.

day_by_day.morning: Visit La Boqueria Market on La Rambla (free entry) – best visited early (9:00–10:30) before the tourist crowds. Browse the colourful stalls of fresh produce, cured meats, and local specialities. Pick up affordable fresh fruit and snacks. Afterwards, explore the nearby MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art) – the building's architecture by Richard Meier is striking and free to admire from outside. The surrounding Raval neighbourhood has excellent street art worth exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the metro or a leisurely walk to Montjuïc. Ride the Telefèric de Montjuïc cable car (€12.70 return) for panoramic views, or hike up for free via the park paths. Visit the free exterior of the Castell de Montjuïc and enjoy the gardens. The Fundació Joan Miró is nearby (~€14 entry) if budget allows, or simply enjoy the free Jardins de Laribal and city views. Return to the city in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Barceloneta and Port Olímpic area for sunset over the Mediterranean. This is a great nightlife hub – Port Olímpic has numerous clubs and bars that get busy after 23:00. For a more local and affordable experience, try the bars along Carrer del Parlament in Sant Antoni neighbourhood, which has a trendy but budget-friendly bar scene.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit and a snack from La Boqueria Market – budget ~€4–6
meals.lunch: Affordable lunch in El Raval – try a menú del día at a local restaurant (many offer €10–12 three-course lunches with wine). Alternatively, a falafel wrap from one of the many Middle Eastern spots in Raval for ~€5.
meals.dinner: Tapas and drinks in Sant Antoni neighbourhood – Bar Calders or similar local spots. Budget ~€10–13.

day_by_day.notes: La Boqueria can be very touristy and overpriced for eating – stick to buying fresh produce rather than prepared food. The Montjuïc area is large; wear comfortable shoes. August evenings are warm so outdoor terraces are perfect for nightlife.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Eixample district on foot – a grid-planned neighbourhood showcasing Barcelona's modernista architecture. Walk along Passeig de Gràcia and spot the free exteriors of Casa Amatller, Casa Lleó Morera, and revisit Casa Batlló and La Pedrera from the outside. Pop into the Mercat de l'Abaceria in Gràcia (free entry) for a local market experience. Visit the free Jardins de la Ciutadella park – a beautiful green space with a lake, fountains, and the impressive Cascada Monumental.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the final afternoon at Barceloneta Beach for a last swim and relaxation. Walk along the Passeig Marítim promenade. Visit the free Barceloneta neighbourhood and its narrow streets. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at affordable spots – avoid La Rambla tourist shops; instead try local shops in El Born or Gràcia for better prices and authentic items. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Barcelona – treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal within budget. Head back to the hotel and prepare luggage for the return journey. If the flight is not early the next morning, enjoy a final stroll in the local Sant Just Desvern area or a quiet drink at a neighbourhood bar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a café con leche and tostada con tomate at a local café – budget ~€3–5. Tostada con tomate (bread rubbed with tomato and olive oil) is a quintessential Catalan breakfast.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Parc de la Ciutadella with supplies from a local supermarket – budget ~€5–7
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on a final dinner – try a traditional Catalan restaurant in El Born or Barceloneta for paella or fideuà. Budget ~€15–20 for a special farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for the afternoon. Keep metro T-Casual card topped up for airport transfer. Total estimated daily spend (excluding accommodation): Day 1 ~€15, Day 2 ~€30, Day 3 ~€55–65, Day 4 ~€40–50, Day 5 ~€30–40. Overall trip budget estimate: ~€170–200 excluding flights and accommodation.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 19:20. Use morning for in-flight rest and preparation.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Still in transit. Arrive at Barcelona Airport (~19:20), clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to Sercotel Porta Barcelona in Sant Just Desvern (~45–60 min by taxi or Aerobus + taxi, approx €30–40). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Casual first-night stroll around Sant Just Desvern's local streets to decompress after travel. Grab a relaxed dinner at a nearby neighbourhood restaurant – no heavy planning tonight. Head to bed early to beat jet lag and prepare for a full Day 2.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: On the plane or at Barcelona El Prat Airport (try a bocadillo or café snack at a terminal café, ~€8–12).
meals.dinner: Restaurant La Bodega de Sant Just or a local tapas bar near the hotel in Sant Just Desvern – simple Catalan dishes like pa amb tomàquet, croquetes, and grilled fish (~€20–28 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Sant Just Desvern is a quiet residential suburb ~10 km from central Barcelona. Taxis to the city centre cost ~€20–25. The L3 metro (Zona Universitària stop) is reachable by a short bus or taxi ride. Keep Day 1 light – rest is the priority. Confirm hotel breakfast times for the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour – Take a taxi or metro into the city (Sagrada Família stop, L2/L5). Arrive early (~9:00–9:30) to beat the August heat and crowds. Enjoy a skip-the-line guided tour of Gaudí's iconic basilica, including tower access for panoramic views over Barcelona's Eixample grid. Allow 2–2.5 hours. The intricate facades, stained glass, and forest-like interior are unmissable for architecture lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Sagrada Família, walk or take a short taxi to the Eixample district and explore the Manzana de la Discordia (Block of Discord) on Passeig de Gràcia – admire Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera from the outside (enter Casa Batlló if budget allows, ~€35). Stroll up Passeig de Gràcia, window-shopping and people-watching. Rest at a shaded café terrace during the hottest part of the afternoon (~14:00–16:00).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Gothic Quarter for the Gothic Quarter Architecture Walk – a self-guided evening stroll (cooler temperatures make this ideal) through Barri Gòtic, discovering Roman walls, the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and hidden medieval passages. The golden-hour light on the stone facades is spectacular. Finish near the waterfront at La Barceloneta for a sea breeze.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Sercotel Porta Barcelona or a café near the hotel (~€8–12). Alternatively, grab a croissant and coffee at a local bakery en route.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca (Eixample) – beloved local spot for montaditos, fresh seafood tapas, and cold beer (~€18–25 per person). Arrive before 13:30 to avoid long queues.
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet in El Born – a classic Catalan cava bar serving anchovies, cheese, and cold cuts with house cava (~€20–28 per person). Lively, authentic atmosphere perfect for a first real Barcelona evening.

day_by_day.notes: August temperatures peak around 29°C – wear light clothing, sunscreen, and carry water. Book Sagrada Família tickets online in advance (€26–33 with tower access). The Gothic Quarter is best explored on foot; wear comfortable shoes. Return to hotel by taxi or metro (L3 to Zona Universitària, then short taxi).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Park Güell – Take a taxi or metro (L3 Lesseps or Vallcarca) to Gaudí's whimsical hilltop park. Arrive at opening time (~9:00) to secure your timed entry to the Monumental Zone (book online, ~€10). Explore the mosaic terrace, Hypostyle Room, and winding viaducts with sweeping views over Barcelona and the sea. The park's organic architecture and colourful trencadís tilework are a highlight for architecture enthusiasts. Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the Gràcia neighbourhood for lunch, then explore this bohemian village-within-a-city. Browse the charming squares (Plaça del Sol, Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia), independent boutiques, and street art. In the late afternoon, head to Montjuïc via cable car or bus for views over the port and city. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró if interested in art (~€14), or simply enjoy the gardens and Castell de Montjuïc terraces.
day_by_day.evening: Tapas Crawl on Carrer del Parlament – Head to the vibrant Sant Antoni neighbourhood for a progressive tapas dinner. Start at Bar Calders for vermouth and olives, move to Bodega Sepúlveda for wine and cheese, and finish at Federal Café or Morro Fi for creative pintxos. This is a lively, local-favourite area with a great mix of traditional and modern Catalan cuisine. The neighbourhood buzzes with energy on summer evenings.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato) at a café in Gràcia after Park Güell (~€5–8).
meals.lunch: La Pepita in Gràcia – trendy spot for creative montaditos and fresh salads in a beautifully tiled space (~€15–22 per person).
meals.dinner: Tapas crawl on Carrer del Parlament, Sant Antoni – budget ~€25–35 per person across 3–4 stops including drinks. Try patatas bravas, jamón ibérico, boquerones, and local craft beer or house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell timed tickets sell out weeks in advance in August – book as early as possible. Montjuïc cable car (Telefèric de Montjuïc) runs from Paral·lel metro station (~€12.70 return). Sant Antoni is easily reached by metro (L2 Sant Antoni stop). The tapas crawl area is walkable and safe at night.

day_by_day.morning: Palau de la Música Catalana Guided Tour – Start the morning with a guided tour of this breathtaking UNESCO-listed Modernista concert hall designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner (~€22, tours run from 9:00). Marvel at the stained-glass skylight, sculpted columns, and ornate facade. This is one of the most extraordinary interiors in all of Europe and a must for architecture lovers. Allow 1–1.5 hours. Afterwards, explore the surrounding El Born neighbourhood – visit the Mercat de Santa Caterina (a colourful alternative to La Boqueria) and browse the boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Barceloneta Beach for a mid-afternoon swim and relaxation (the sea temperature in August is around 25°C – perfect). Rent a sun lounger (~€6–8) or find a free spot. Walk along the Passeig Marítim promenade and explore the Port Olímpic area. Visit the Frank Gehry's golden Fish sculpture and the twin Olympic towers. As the heat eases (~17:00–18:00), explore the Poblenou neighbourhood – Barcelona's creative tech district with street art and converted industrial spaces.
day_by_day.evening: Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert – Return to the Palau de la Música for a live evening concert in this magnificent hall. Check the August programme online (tickets ~€25–60 depending on performance – classical, flamenco, and jazz concerts are common). Experiencing music inside this luminous space at night is an unforgettable, uniquely Barcelonan experience. Dress smart-casual.

meals.breakfast: Café de l'Acadèmia near the Gothic Quarter – classic Catalan breakfast with coffee, toast, and fresh orange juice (~€7–10).
meals.lunch: La Cova Fumada in Barceloneta (cash only, arrives early as it sells out) – legendary local spot, birthplace of the bombas (meat croquettes). Simple, fresh, and authentic (~€15–20 per person).
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Bar del Pla in El Born – excellent Catalan cuisine with dishes like duck confit, fresh pasta, and local wines (~€25–35 per person). Conveniently close to the Palau de la Música.

day_by_day.notes: Book Palau de la Música concert tickets well in advance via palaumusica.cat – August is peak season and performances sell out. The guided morning tour and evening concert can be combined on the same day efficiently. La Cova Fumada opens only for lunch and closes when food runs out – arrive by 13:00. Barceloneta can be very crowded in August; go mid-afternoon rather than midday.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning – Sleep in and enjoy a relaxed hotel breakfast. Pack any souvenirs and do a final walk around Sant Just Desvern or take a short taxi to the nearby Parc de Cervantes (rose garden, free entry) for a peaceful morning stroll. Alternatively, head into the city one last time to revisit a favourite neighbourhood or pick up last-minute gifts at the Mercat de Sant Antoni (open Monday–Saturday, great for vintage books, local products, and crafts).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to central Barcelona for a final afternoon of exploration. Visit the Fundació Antoni Tàpies in Eixample (Modernista building with contemporary Catalan art, ~€12) or simply wander Passeig de Gràcia one last time for photos. Stop at Escribà patisserie for artisan chocolates and pastries to take home. Begin making your way back to the hotel to collect luggage and prepare for departure (check flight details for Day 6 or later).
day_by_day.evening: Razzmatazz Club Night – Go out with a bang at Barcelona's legendary Razzmatazz club in Poblenou (five rooms, multiple music genres from indie to techno and electronic). Doors open around 23:30–00:00; the club peaks between 02:00–05:00. Entry ~€15–20 (check for online presale discounts). This is one of Europe's top club experiences and a perfect finale for a trip that balances architecture by day with nightlife by night. Dress comfortably but stylishly; lockers available inside.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café in Sant Just Desvern – enjoy a slow café amb llet and croissant (~€5–8).
meals.lunch: Parking Pizza in Eixample – beloved local pizzeria with creative toppings and natural wines in a relaxed setting (~€18–25 per person). A great casual farewell lunch.
meals.dinner: Pre-club dinner at Bodega Sepúlveda in Sant Antoni or Rasoterra (vegetarian Catalan, El Gòtic) for a lighter, healthy meal before a late night (~€22–30 per person). Eat early (~20:00–21:00) to have energy for the club.

day_by_day.notes: Razzmatazz is located at Carrer dels Almogàvers 122, Poblenou – easily reached by taxi (~€10–12 from city centre) or metro (L4 Bogatell). The club runs until 06:00; plan accordingly if you have an early departure the next day. Keep valuables secure and use the cloakroom. August nights in Barcelona are warm (~22–24°C), so light clothing is fine even late at night. Confirm hotel late check-out or luggage storage if needed.

A pre-arranged private luxury transfer (Mercedes E-Class or similar) whisks you to Sercotel Porta Barcelona in Sant Just Desvern. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the quiet residential neighbourhood to decompress after travel.

meals.lunch: N/A – in transit or airport lounge dining
meals.dinner: Late dinner at El Celler de Can Roca's sister concept or, closer to the hotel, Restaurant La Cantonada (Sant Just Desvern) – a refined Catalan bistro serving seasonal tasting menus with excellent local wine pairings. Reserve ahead for a 21:30 seating.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Confirm private airport transfer in advance. The hotel concierge should be briefed to have welcome amenities (Cava, local charcuterie) ready in the room. August evenings are warm (~24°C), so light linen clothing is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour – Begin the day with a skip-the-line premium guided tour of Gaudí's iconic basilica. Opt for the full experience including tower access (Nativity and Passion towers) for sweeping panoramic views over Barcelona. Arrive at opening time (~09:00) to beat the August crowds. A private guide adds architectural context that transforms the visit from sightseeing into a genuine cultural immersion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gothic Quarter Architecture Walk – After lunch, take a chauffeured transfer into the old city and embark on a small-group or private guided walk through the Barri Gòtic. Discover Roman walls, the medieval Cathedral of Barcelona, Plaça Reial, and hidden courtyards. The narrow stone lanes are cooler in the afternoon shade, making this the ideal time slot in August heat.
day_by_day.evening: Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert – Conclude the day inside Lluís Domènech i Montaner's breathtaking UNESCO-listed Modernista concert hall. Attend a live classical or flamenco performance beneath the iconic stained-glass skylight. Dress smart-casual; the venue itself is the spectacle.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a visit to a nearby artisan café for pa amb tomàquet, fresh orange juice, and a cortado.
meals.lunch: Lasarte (3 Michelin stars, near Passeig de Gràcia) – Martin Berasategui's Barcelona flagship. Book well in advance. Tasting menu with wine pairing is the definitive luxury midday experience.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert light dinner at Bar Calders or Bodega Sepúlveda in Sant Antoni – elegant pintxos and natural wines – keeping it relaxed before the evening performance. Alternatively, enjoy the Palau's own champagne bar during the interval.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tower access and Palau de la Música tickets months in advance for August. Lasarte requires reservations 4–6 weeks ahead minimum. Private car or taxi recommended between Sagrada Família and Gothic Quarter (~15 min).

day_by_day.morning: Casa Batlló & Passeig de Gràcia Modernisme Walk – Explore the 'Block of Discord' on Passeig de Gràcia, visiting Casa Batlló with the premium Magic Nights or daytime immersive experience (augmented reality included). Stroll past Casa Amatller and Casa Lleó Morera. The boulevard itself is a living museum of Catalan Modernisme architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Palau Güell & El Raval Exploration – Walk or transfer to Palau Güell, Gaudí's early masterpiece near the Ramblas. The rooftop chimneys offer a quieter, more intimate Gaudí experience than the Sagrada Família. Afterwards, explore the MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art) exterior and the emerging creative scene of El Raval neighbourhood.
day_by_day.evening: Razzmatazz Club Night – Experience Barcelona's legendary nightclub, one of Europe's finest, with five distinct rooms spanning electronic, indie, and pop. Doors open around 01:00 for the serious crowd; arrive fashionably late. VIP table or booth reservation strongly recommended for a luxury experience with bottle service.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at Federal Café (El Raval) or Parking Pizza's brunch – avocado toast, eggs Benedict, fresh juices in a stylish setting.
meals.lunch: Tickets (Albert Adrià's avant-garde tapas bar, El Poble Sec) – a theatrical, Michelin-starred tapas experience. Book online the moment reservations open (60 days in advance).
meals.dinner: Late dinner at Bodega 1900 (also Albert Adrià, nearby Tickets) – a sophisticated vermouth bar and restaurant serving elevated traditional Catalan dishes. Perfect pre-club fuel around 22:00.

day_by_day.notes: Razzmatazz is open until 06:00. Plan for a late start the following morning. Dress code is stylish but not formal. Pre-book VIP entry or table service through the club's official website or a concierge service. Uber/Cabify recommended for late-night return to hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Late, Leisurely Morning Recovery – After the Razzmatazz night, allow a slow start. Enjoy a late hotel breakfast or head to a nearby specialty coffee shop. Optional: visit the Fundació Joan Miró on Montjuïc (opens 10:00) for world-class modern art in a stunning rationalist building by Josep Lluís Sert – a quieter, culturally rich alternative to the busier Gaudí sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montjuïc & Pavilion Mies van der Rohe – Explore the Montjuïc hill by cable car or private car. Visit the Barcelona Pavilion (Mies van der Rohe, 1929) – a pilgrimage site for architecture lovers, featuring the iconic Barcelona Chair in its original setting. Continue to the Jardins de Laribal for shaded terraced gardens with city views. The Olympic Stadium exterior and Palau Sant Jordi (Arata Isozaki) round out an afternoon of landmark 20th-century architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Tapas Crawl on Carrer del Parlament – Recover your appetite with a curated tapas crawl through the vibrant Sant Antoni neighbourhood. Begin with vermouth at Bar Calders, move to patatas bravas and jamón at Bodega Sepúlveda, and finish with fresh seafood pintxos at a neighbourhood favourite. The area buzzes with a sophisticated local crowd on summer evenings.

meals.breakfast: Late breakfast at the hotel or Nomad Coffee Lab (Eixample) – specialty single-origin coffee and pastries.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Fundació Joan Miró café terrace, or a charcuterie and cheese board at a Montjuïc viewpoint restaurant.
meals.dinner: The tapas crawl on Carrer del Parlament IS dinner – budget €40–60 per person across 3–4 stops including drinks. End the evening with a nightcap at Bar Calders or a rooftop bar in Eixample.

day_by_day.notes: Montjuïc is best explored with a private driver or the Montjuïc cable car (Telefèric de Montjuïc). Book Fundació Joan Miró tickets online. The Barcelona Pavilion is often uncrowded mid-week – a genuine architectural gem. Sant Antoni tapas bars fill up after 21:00; no reservations needed, just walk in.

day_by_day.morning: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighbourhood – Visit Park Güell early (09:00 entry, pre-booked timed ticket required for the Monumental Zone) to enjoy Gaudí's mosaic terraces and the iconic hypostyle hall before the August heat peaks. The views over Barcelona from the main terrace are spectacular. Afterwards, descend into the charming Gràcia neighbourhood – a village within the city – for a wander through its plaças and independent boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Casa Vicens (Gaudí's First House) & Eixample Modernisme – Visit Casa Vicens, Gaudí's very first major work (recently opened to the public), tucked in Gràcia. Then transfer to the Eixample grid for a self-guided walk admiring the Modernista pharmacy facades, lampposts, and hexagonal pavement tiles. Optional: interior visit to Casa Milà (La Pedrera) rooftop for sunset views – book the premium 'La Pedrera by Night' experience if timing allows.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Luxury Dinner & Optional Late Nightlife – Celebrate the final evening with a world-class dinner, then optionally extend into Barcelona's nightlife scene for a final taste of the city after dark.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before Park Güell. Alternatively, pick up a croissant and coffee at a Gràcia neighbourhood bakery post-visit.
meals.lunch: La Pepita (Gràcia) – a beautifully designed restaurant in a former hat shop, serving creative Catalan-Mediterranean cuisine. Perfect post-Park Güell lunch in a stunning interior.
meals.dinner: Disfrutar (2 Michelin stars, recently ranked #1 in The World's 50 Best Restaurants) – an unmissable avant-garde tasting menu by three former elBulli chefs. This is the pinnacle of Barcelona fine dining. Reserve 2–3 months in advance. Wine pairing is exceptional. Budget €250–350 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell timed tickets sell out weeks in advance in August – book immediately upon planning. La Pedrera by Night is a magical experience if you can secure tickets. Disfrutar is arguably the hardest reservation in Barcelona; use the hotel concierge or a restaurant reservation service. If departing the following morning, arrange a private transfer the night before and confirm checkout time with the hotel.

query: Barcelona architecture and nightlife, $2000, 5 days, August from NYC
